title: Macroeconomic Risks from Maritime Trade Disruptions
abstract: arXiv:2607.09951v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper develops a model of maritime chokepoint closures in which interrupting a shipping passage produces losses that are not measured, or even bounded, by the value of the trade that transits it. The losses stem from disruptions to the flow of intermediate inputs that are complementary in downstream production. Re-matching displaced trade on the buyer and seller sides of the market limits the damage but, at the calibrated recovery friction, does not eliminate it. Across countries, the incidence of these losses is heavy-tailed, and it reaches economies whose cargo never crosses the passage. The two ends of a severed corridor lose unequally, the exporting side by several times at the typical corridor and by a factor of twelve at the largest energy gate, as economic geography funnels commodity-concentrated sellers through a single passage while their buyers re-source. translated_title: 海上贸易中断的宏观经济风险
translated_abstract: 本文建立了一个关于海上咽喉要道关闭的模型，在该模型中，中断一条航运通道所造成的损失，既不由经过该通道的贸易价值来衡量，甚至也不受其限制。这些损失源于对下游生产中具有互补性的中间投入品流动的破坏。市场买卖双方对被中断贸易的重新匹配能够限制损害，但按校准的恢复摩擦参数来看，并不能完全消除损害。从各国来看，这些损失的分布呈厚尾特征，并且会波及那些货物从未经过该通道的经济体。被切断的走廊两端所承受的损失并不均等，在典型走廊上出口方的损失是进口方的数倍，而在最大的能源门户处更是高达十二倍，这是因为经济地理因素将商品集中的卖家经由单一通道汇集，而其买家则会重新寻找货源。海上咽喉要道的联合关闭所造成的影响超出了它们各自单独关闭的总和。
tldr: 本文建立海上咽喉要道关闭模型，揭示航运通道中断造成的经济损失可能远超经过该通道的贸易价值，损失在各国间呈厚尾分布并波及非过境经济体，且出口方承受的损失可达进口方的数倍甚至十二倍。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a model of maritime chokepoint closures showing that disrupting a shipping passage causes losses exceeding the value of transiting trade, with heavy-tailed incidence across countries reaching non-transiting economies, and exporters bearing losses up to twelve times those of importers at the largest energy gate.
